title: The canonical coefficient morphisms $\alpha_f$, $\eta_f$
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a condensed ring, let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of
schemes, and let $\Lambda_X$, $\Lambda_Y$ be the pulled-back coefficient rings
of [det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The pullback
$f^*\Lambda_Y$ and the pushforward $f_*\Lambda_X$ are ring objects: $f^*$ is
strong monoidal ([def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal]) and $f_*$ is lax monoidal
([def-sfb-finite-lower-star-lax-monoidal]). Define
$$
\alpha_f\colon f^*\Lambda_Y\longrightarrow\Lambda_X,\qquad
\eta_f\colon\Lambda_Y\longrightarrow f_*\Lambda_X
$$
as follows.

- $\alpha_f$ is the component at $\Lambda$ of the natural isomorphism
  $f^*\circ p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ of [det-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp].
- $\eta_f$ is the mate of $\alpha_f$ under the adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$
  ([def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction]): the
  unit $\Lambda_Y\to f_*f^*\Lambda_Y$ followed by $f_*\alpha_f$.

Both are morphisms of ring objects. Moreover, $\alpha_f$ underlies an
isomorphism of ring objects $f^*\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_X$.

proof.text: By [det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ with $p_X^*=\pi_X^*\circ p^*$ of [det-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], part 4, and $p^*=\mathrm{sheafify}\circ\operatorname{Lan}_{u^{\mathrm{op}}}$ of part 3. This is literally the functor $p_X^*$ of [def-sfb-upper-star-from-point], whose $p^*$ is the same composite ([def-sfb-point-upper-star]) and whose $\pi_X^*$ is the same pullback of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star]. The ring structure of $\Lambda_X$ in [det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] is the transport $\mu_X=p_X^*(\mu)\circ\mu^{p_X^*}_{\Lambda,\Lambda}$, $\eta_X=p_X^*(\eta)\circ\varepsilon^{p_X^*}$ of clause 1 of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport], word for word the ring object $\Lambda_X$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] used in the statements of the cited child nodes. Likewise the ring structures on $f^*\Lambda_Y$ and $f_*\Lambda_X$ named in the statement are those of clause 1 of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport] for $F=f^*$ with the strong structure of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal] and $F=f_*$ with the lax structure of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-lax-monoidal], specialized to $\mathcal A=\Ab$.

The comparison $c_f\colon f^*\circ p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ of [det-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp] is, by its statement, $p^*$ composed with the inverse of the composition isomorphism $(\pi_Y\circ f)^*\cong f^*\circ\pi_Y^*$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-comp], followed by the identification $(\pi_Y\circ f)^*=\pi_X^*$. By step 1 the functors $p^*$, $p_X^*$, $p_Y^*$ are those of [def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso], whose statement defines its natural isomorphism by exactly this composite. So $c_f$ is the isomorphism of [def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso], and [def-sfb-alpha] says that its component at $\Lambda$ is $\alpha_f\colon f^*\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_X$. [lem-sfb-alpha-ring-hom] says that $\alpha_f$ is a morphism of ring objects for the ring structure on $f^*\Lambda_Y$ transported along $f^*$ fixed in step 1.

[def-sfb-alpha-bundled] gives an isomorphism of ring objects $f^*\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_X$, the composite of the identification of $f^*$ applied to the ring object $p_Y^*\Lambda$ with the ring object $(f^*\circ p_Y^*)\Lambda$, followed by the component $c_f(\Lambda)$ of step 2. Write $F=p_Y^*$ and $G=f^*$. By the definition of the composite lax monoidal structure, both transported multiplications are $GF(\mu)\circ G(\mu^F_{\Lambda,\Lambda})\circ\mu^G_{F\Lambda,F\Lambda}$ and both units are $GF(\eta)\circ G(\varepsilon^F)\circ\varepsilon^G$, so the first identification has underlying map $\mathrm{id}_{GF\Lambda}$. Hence the underlying morphism of the bundled isomorphism is $c_f(\Lambda)=\alpha_f$: $\alpha_f$ underlies an isomorphism of ring objects.

Let $u\colon\mathrm{id}\to f_*f^*$ be the unit of the adjunction of [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction] for $\mathcal A=\Ab$. [def-sfb-eta] defines $\eta_f=f_*(\alpha_f)\circ u_{\Lambda_Y}\colon\Lambda_Y\to f_*\Lambda_X$, the mate of $\alpha_f$, with $\alpha_f$ as in step 2; this is the map of the statement. [lem-sfb-eta-ring-hom] says that $\eta_f$ is a morphism of ring objects for the ring structure on $f_*\Lambda_X$ induced by the lax structure of $f_*$, which is the structure fixed in step 1.

The degenerate cases (identity f, empty X) are fine. There are no new nodes.
